advisories.title: "DR-105 law" understates that the self-grant sentence sits in a PROPOSED section
advisories.finding: The subject writes: 'File 03's permission section says a publisher cannot grant authority to itself. That sentence is DR-105 law.' The sentence exists and is faithfully characterized — file 03 lines 98-99 read 'A manifest, repository, or publisher cannot grant authority to itself' (narrowing the three-actor list to 'publisher' is a faithful subset for this row, and the field does not claim verbatim carry). The ownership routing is also correct: line 98 sits inside '## Proposed permissions with honest outcomes' (lines 91-128), which is exactly DR-105's register anchor. What is missing is file 03's own maturity hedge at lines 126-127 — 'This is a proposed V2 mechanism at DR-105, not evidence that any current platform enforces it' — and the section heading's own word, 'Proposed'. The subject uses 'law' consistently elsewhere to mean 'owned by row N' (ID-DEP-T1's 'DR-117 law'), and there the referent IS an in-force default (file 03's PRESERVED confinement section: marketplace 'remain[s] excluded by default'). The asymmetry is that here the referent is a proposal at an OPEN row.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The routing conclusion — DR-105 owns it, DR-116 does not re-own it — is correct regardless of proposed-versus-enforced. The error direction is disclaiming authority, not taking it. The artifact binds NOTHING, is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED / DO-NOT-SEAL, and this field changes no disposition, no status token, and no acceptance evidence.
advisories.owedTo: A successor, as wording precision: qualify the sentence as file 03's PROPOSED V2 mechanism at DR-105 per lines 126-127, so the proposed-versus-enforced discipline this corpus enforces is not loosened by the word 'law'.
